what_it_does: This position paper addresses a fundamental bottleneck in AI systems called the 'memory wall'—the growing gap between how fast a processor's computing units can do math and how fast the memory system can deliver data to them. Traditional memory architectures (built over decades for general computing) cannot keep up with AI's voracious demand for bandwidth, latency, and capacity. The paper argues that memory innovations are essential to AI's future and outlines multiple solution directions: new memory technologies are being developed and gradually integrated into shipping products to help bridge this compute-memory gap and unlock new AI algorithms.
